contexts.text: He wanted to be trodden under foot by others, which he called Christian patience.
To tread the mire () = falsities. ( = from evil to think falsity. AC 6669:2.)
The signification of treading grapes. AE 376:6.
To tread the sea with horses () = to instruct the natural man.
To tread upon serpents and scorpions () = to destroy evils, and the falsities of evil.
The winepress was trodden without the city () = exploration effected from the Divine truths of the Word. ( = the bringing forth of falsity from evil out of Hell. AE 922.)

He treadeth the winepress of the fury and anger of God Almighty () = that the Lord endured alone all the evils of the Church, and all the violence offered to the Word... To tread the press of this wine = to endure them, to fight against them, and to condemn them; and thus to deliver the Angels and men from infestation by them.
When the thought advances no further, they appear to tread... and not to make progress.
To tread upon the lion, adder, serpents, and scorpions = not only to destroy the evils and falsities which are meant by these, but also not to be harmed by them. Illustrated.
To tread the winepress = to bring forth truth from good; in the opposite, to bring forth falsity from evil. AE 922:2, Illustrated.
